taxa.name: Sahelanthropus tchadensis
taxa.meaning: A late Miocene candidate near the origin of hominins.
taxa.note: Its place near the human–chimpanzee split remains debated; age alone cannot establish direct ancestry.

taxa.name: Orrorin tugenensis
taxa.meaning: Early hominin candidate represented by teeth and limb bones.
taxa.note: Femoral anatomy suggests bipedality; its relationship to later lineages remains unresolved.

taxa.name: Ardipithecus kadabba
taxa.meaning: An early Ethiopian hominin identified mainly from fragmentary remains.
taxa.note: A proposed relationship to Ar. ramidus is not a demonstrated ancestor–descendant chain.

taxa.name: Ardipithecus ramidus
taxa.meaning: A hominin combining climbing and bipedal traits.
taxa.note: Ancestral relationships with Australopithecus are hypotheses; Ardi is an individual, not a species origin date.

taxa.name: Australopithecus anamensis
taxa.meaning: An early species of Australopithecus.
taxa.note: Often linked to A. afarensis; fossil ages and similarities do not identify a particular direct ancestor.

taxa.name: Australopithecus afarensis
taxa.meaning: The East African species including Lucy and Selam.
taxa.note: A candidate near later hominin ancestry; contemporary diversity leaves its precise relationships open.

taxa.name: Australopithecus bahrelghazali
taxa.meaning: A name for a small Pliocene hominin sample from Chad.
taxa.note: Its separation from other australopith species is debated; a western occurrence is not a migration route.

taxa.name: Kenyanthropus platyops
taxa.meaning: A proposed flat-faced hominin from West Turkana.
taxa.note: Distortion of the principal cranium complicates taxonomic interpretation.

taxa.name: Australopithecus deyiremeda
taxa.meaning: A proposed australopith contemporary of A. afarensis.
taxa.note: Jaws, teeth and an attributed foot broaden known diversity without proving ancestry of Homo.

taxa.name: Australopithecus africanus
taxa.meaning: A southern African australopith species.
taxa.note: Its connection to Homo and the ages and assignments of some cave fossils remain debated.

taxa.name: Australopithecus garhi
taxa.meaning: An australopith named from Bouri cranial remains.
taxa.note: Nearby limb and butchered-animal remains do not securely identify its behavior or descendants.

taxa.name: Australopithecus sediba
taxa.meaning: A Malapa hominin with a mosaic of australopith and Homo-like features.
taxa.note: A proposed connection to Homo does not make the known Malapa individuals ancestors of older Homo fossils.

taxa.name: Paranthropus, species unresolved
taxa.meaning: Robust-chewing hominins identified to genus only.
taxa.note: A genus-level tooth identification cannot be assigned automatically to a named species.

taxa.name: Paranthropus aethiopicus
taxa.meaning: An early robust-chewing lineage in eastern Africa.
taxa.note: Its relationships with other Paranthropus species are reconstructed from fragmentary morphology.

taxa.name: Paranthropus boisei
taxa.meaning: An eastern African lineage with specialized chewing anatomy.
taxa.note: It overlapped with Homo; archaeological association does not identify every toolmaker.

taxa.name: Paranthropus robustus
taxa.meaning: A southern African robust-chewing lineage.
taxa.note: The word robust describes chewing anatomy, not a demonstrated evolutionary stage toward us.

taxa.name: Early Homo, species unresolved
taxa.meaning: Fossils assigned to Homo without a secure species identification.
taxa.note: This is a catalogue grouping, not another named species or an ancestor asserted for all later Homo.

taxa.name: Homo habilis
taxa.meaning: A named early Homo species anchored by Olduvai material.
taxa.note: Its fossil membership and relationships to erectus and rudolfensis remain debated.

taxa.name: Homo rudolfensis
taxa.meaning: An early Homo name associated with KNM-ER 1470.
taxa.note: Species boundaries and the association of isolated jaws with cranial fossils remain uncertain.

taxa.name: Homo erectus, broadly defined
taxa.meaning: A widespread early Homo grouping in Africa and Eurasia.
taxa.note: African material is sometimes called H. ergaster and Dmanisi material H. georgicus; this broad label does not settle those classifications.

taxa.name: Homo antecessor
taxa.meaning: Early Pleistocene Homo from Gran Dolina.
taxa.note: Enamel proteins support a close sister relationship to later Homo ancestry, not a proven direct ancestor.

taxa.name: Homo heidelbergensis
taxa.meaning: A name anchored by the Mauer mandible.
taxa.note: Narrow and broad definitions group different Middle Pleistocene fossils; no single accepted lineage connects them all.

taxa.name: Homo neanderthalensis / Neanderthal lineage
taxa.meaning: A western Eurasian lineage also documented in the Altai.
taxa.note: Some early lineage members predate classic Neanderthal anatomy. Parts of their ancestry survive in living humans.

taxa.name: Denisovans
taxa.meaning: A molecularly identified, internally diverse Asian hominin lineage.
taxa.note: Genetic lineage and proposed fossil species names do not map neatly one to one. Present-day inherited DNA does not locate each ancient encounter.

taxa.name: Homo naledi
taxa.meaning: A small-brained Homo lineage known from the Rising Star cave system.
taxa.note: Its Middle Pleistocene survival and anatomical mosaic do not establish direct ancestry or a genetic contribution to living people.

taxa.name: Homo floresiensis
taxa.meaning: A small-bodied Homo lineage named at Liang Bua on Flores.
taxa.note: Mata Menge fossils suggest a much older related island population; ancestry, arrival route and ultimate disappearance remain incompletely resolved.

taxa.name: Homo luzonensis
taxa.meaning: A named hominin from Callao Cave on Luzon.
taxa.note: Its relationships to other island and mainland hominins are unresolved; morphology alone cannot demonstrate admixture.

taxa.name: Homo sapiens
taxa.meaning: The only hominin species living today.
taxa.note: Early African fossils and later genetic evidence describe structured populations with some archaic admixture, not an isolated ladder of progress.

evidence.title: Toros-Menalla: Sahelanthropus
evidence.dateBasis: Approximate geological age from cosmogenic sediment dating and fossil context. Internal years use 1950 minus the quoted age in years for display; rounded geological ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: Chadian cranial and dental fossils extend early hominin research beyond eastern and southern Africa.
evidence.limits: A rounded occurrence anchor, not the date of the human–chimpanzee split or proof of direct ancestry. Coordinates mark an approximate public locality, not a surveyed fossil position.

evidence.title: Tugen Hills: Orrorin
evidence.dateBasis: Published geological age range of the regional fossil sample. Internal years use 1950 minus the quoted age in years for display; rounded geological ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: Lukeino Formation teeth and limb bones include femora interpreted as showing bipedal loading.
evidence.limits: Grouped regional localities; fossils do not demonstrate continuous occupation throughout the interval. Coordinates mark an approximate public locality, not a surveyed fossil position.

evidence.title: Middle Awash: Ardipithecus kadabba
evidence.dateBasis: Range covers several dated fossil occurrences, not a single occupation. Internal years use 1950 minus the quoted age in years for display; rounded geological ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: Teeth and fragmentary bones, including a younger attributed toe bone, document an early hominin form.
evidence.limits: The toe and older fossils are separated in locality and age; the grouping is not a single skeleton. Coordinates mark an approximate public locality, not a surveyed fossil position.

evidence.title: Aramis: Ardi and Ardipithecus ramidus
evidence.dateBasis: Rounded age of the Aramis fossil-bearing deposits. Internal years use 1950 minus the quoted age in years for display; rounded geological ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: Ardi preserves a combination of climbing-related anatomy and features relevant to upright movement.
evidence.limits: Reconstruction of crushed bones and interpretation of locomotion carry uncertainty. Coordinates mark an approximate public locality, not a surveyed fossil position.

evidence.title: Kanapoi: Australopithecus anamensis
evidence.dateBasis: Approximate age of the Kanapoi fossil-bearing sequence. Internal years use 1950 minus the quoted age in years for display; rounded geological ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: Teeth, jaws and a tibia document an early Australopithecus population with bipedal adaptations.
evidence.limits: This locality is one observation within the species range, not its demonstrated birthplace. Coordinates mark an approximate public locality, not a surveyed fossil position.

evidence.title: Laetoli: preserved bipedal steps
evidence.dateBasis: Rounded geological age of the footprint-bearing volcanic deposits. Internal years use 1950 minus the quoted age in years for display; rounded geological ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: Footprint trails preserve walking behavior and are commonly attributed to A. afarensis.
evidence.limits: The principal trackmaker attribution is inferred from anatomy and nearby fossils; footprints are not DNA or a named individual. Coordinates mark an approximate public locality, not a surveyed fossil position.

evidence.title: Koro Toro: Australopithecus in Chad
evidence.dateBasis: Quoted cosmogenic age and uncertainty for KT12 sediments. Internal years use 1950 minus the quoted age in years for display; rounded geological ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: The Abel jaw and associated material broaden the known Pliocene hominin distribution west of the Rift.
evidence.limits: The interval expresses published sediment-date uncertainty, not the species lifespan; taxonomy remains debated. Coordinates mark an approximate public locality, not a surveyed fossil position.

evidence.title: Lomekwi: Kenyanthropus platyops
evidence.dateBasis: Rounded fossil-context age; distinct from archaeological tool horizons. Internal years use 1950 minus the quoted age in years for display; rounded geological ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: A distorted cranium and other remains underpin a proposed hominin with a relatively flat face.
evidence.limits: The evidence does not identify who made the separately documented Lomekwi stone tools. Coordinates mark an approximate public locality, not a surveyed fossil position.

evidence.title: Woranso-Mille: a contemporary of Lucy’s species
evidence.dateBasis: Fossil-bearing horizons bracketed by geological dating; rounded range. Internal years use 1950 minus the quoted age in years for display; rounded geological ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: Jaws and teeth support a distinct proposed australopith; a 2025 study also attributes the Burtele foot to this species.
evidence.limits: The regional sample does not identify direct ancestry of Homo or a single continuous population. Coordinates mark an approximate public locality, not a surveyed fossil position.

evidence.title: Dikika: Selam
evidence.dateBasis: Rounded geological age of the juvenile skeleton’s horizon. Internal years use 1950 minus the quoted age in years for display; rounded geological ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: A juvenile skeleton preserves additional anatomy of Lucy’s species.
evidence.limits: One juvenile does not represent all variation in the species. Coordinates mark an approximate public locality, not a surveyed fossil position.

evidence.title: Hadar: Lucy, AL 288-1
evidence.dateBasis: Rounded age of the Kada Hadar Member fossil horizon. Internal years use 1950 minus the quoted age in years for display; rounded geological ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: Lucy’s partial adult skeleton preserves pelvis and limb anatomy of a biped that also retained climbing-related traits.
evidence.limits: The 1974 discovery date is separate from the fossil age; Lucy is not established as a direct ancestor. Coordinates mark an approximate public locality, not a surveyed fossil position.

evidence.title: Sterkfontein: disputed australopith chronology
evidence.dateLabel: Member 4: competing estimates near 3.4–3.5 Ma or 2.6–2.1 Ma
evidence.dateBasis: Explicit display envelope spanning older cosmogenic and younger chronology interpretations for Member 4; no consensus point date. Internal years use 1950 minus the quoted age in years for display; rounded geological ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: Rich southern African cave assemblages preserve australopith diversity. Cosmogenic dates place Member 4 substantially earlier than some previous chronologies.
evidence.limits: The plotted envelope combines competing age interpretations, not a statistical confidence interval or continuous occupation; some fossil assignments also differ. Coordinates mark an approximate public locality, not a surveyed fossil position.

evidence.title: Nyayanga: Paranthropus teeth with Oldowan activity
evidence.dateBasis: Published bracket for the fossil and archaeological sequence; approximate locality cluster. Internal years use 1950 minus the quoted age in years for display; rounded geological ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: Large molars assigned to Paranthropus occur in an archaeological landscape with stone tools and butchered animals.
evidence.limits: The teeth do not establish that Paranthropus made the tools or identify a named species. Coordinates mark an approximate public locality, not a surveyed fossil position.

evidence.title: Ledi-Geraru: LD 350-1 early Homo
evidence.dateBasis: Published stratigraphic age bracket for the mandible. Internal years use 1950 minus the quoted age in years for display; rounded geological ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: A partial mandible combines more ancestral jaw traits with dental features supporting assignment to Homo.
evidence.limits: Genus-level identification does not make it H. habilis or establish the origin date of Homo. Coordinates mark an approximate public locality, not a surveyed fossil position.

evidence.title: West Turkana: the Black Skull
evidence.dateBasis: Rounded published fossil age. Internal years use 1950 minus the quoted age in years for display; rounded geological ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: KNM-WT 17000 preserves pronounced chewing adaptations in an early Paranthropus form.
evidence.limits: Relationships to other robust-chewing species remain reconstructed rather than genetically demonstrated. Coordinates mark an approximate public locality, not a surveyed fossil position.

evidence.title: Bouri: Australopithecus garhi
evidence.dateBasis: Rounded age of the fossil-bearing Hata Member. Internal years use 1950 minus the quoted age in years for display; rounded geological ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: A small cranial sample from the Hata Member defines A. garhi.
evidence.limits: Nearby cut-marked animal bones and limb remains cannot be assigned automatically to the named cranium. Coordinates mark an approximate public locality, not a surveyed fossil position.

evidence.title: Drimolen: early erectus and Paranthropus
evidence.dateBasis: U-Pb flowstone dates, US-ESR tooth dates and palaeomagnetic stratigraphy constrain deposition. Internal years use 1950 minus the quoted age in years for display; rounded geological ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: DNH 134 has erectus affinities; DNH 152 represents P. robustus in the same quarry sequence.
evidence.limits: A juvenile skullcap carries taxonomic uncertainty; contemporaneity in a deposit is not evidence of interbreeding. Coordinates mark an approximate public locality, not a surveyed fossil position.

evidence.title: Malapa: Australopithecus sediba
evidence.dateBasis: Published narrow geological bracket for the Malapa assemblage. Internal years use 1950 minus the quoted age in years for display; rounded geological ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: Partial skeletons reveal a mosaic of anatomical traits in a late australopith population.
evidence.limits: Homo-like features do not prove these individuals gave rise to Homo; known Homo material is older. Coordinates mark an approximate public locality, not a surveyed fossil position.

evidence.title: Koobi Fora: KNM-ER 1470
evidence.dateBasis: Rounded fossil age published by the Smithsonian. Internal years use 1950 minus the quoted age in years for display; rounded geological ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: A relatively large-brained early Homo cranium anchors discussion of H. rudolfensis.
evidence.limits: The species distinction from H. habilis is debated; isolated jaws cannot be matched with certainty. Coordinates mark an approximate public locality, not a surveyed fossil position.

evidence.title: Olduvai Gorge: Homo habilis type material
evidence.dateBasis: Rounded age of the type-area material, not the full species range. Internal years use 1950 minus the quoted age in years for display; rounded geological ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: OH 7 and associated research at Olduvai helped define Homo habilis.
evidence.limits: Species membership of other early Homo fragments and the identity of particular toolmakers remain open. Coordinates mark an approximate public locality, not a surveyed fossil position.

evidence.title: Olduvai Gorge: OH 5 Paranthropus boisei
evidence.dateBasis: Rounded age of the OH 5 fossil horizon. Internal years use 1950 minus the quoted age in years for display; rounded geological ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: The OH 5 cranium preserves the distinctive chewing apparatus of P. boisei.
evidence.limits: Its occurrence alongside archaeological material is not proof that this species manufactured each tool. Coordinates mark an approximate public locality, not a surveyed fossil position.

evidence.title: Dmanisi: early Eurasian Homo fossils
evidence.dateBasis: Approximate fossil-bearing stratum B interval; older tools at 1.85–1.78 Ma are a different observation. Internal years use 1950 minus the quoted age in years for display; rounded geological ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: Multiple crania and other remains document early Homo outside Africa; archaeological occupations at the locality began earlier.
evidence.limits: The grouping includes fossils also called H. georgicus. It does not establish the first Eurasian arrival or a migration route. Coordinates mark an approximate public locality, not a surveyed fossil position.

evidence.title: Gran Dolina: Homo antecessor
evidence.dateBasis: Published ESR/U-series and contextual age bracket for the sampled tooth. Internal years use 1950 minus the quoted age in years for display; rounded geological ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: Enamel proteins place this Gran Dolina hominin close to the common ancestry of later Homo lineages.
evidence.limits: Limited informative protein sites do not reconstruct a full genome or prove direct ancestry. Coordinates mark an approximate public locality, not a surveyed fossil position.

evidence.title: Mata Menge: early small-bodied Flores hominins
evidence.dateBasis: Rounded age of the fossil-bearing deposit. Internal years use 1950 minus the quoted age in years for display; rounded geological ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: Small teeth, jaws and an adult humerus suggest a much older history for the Flores island lineage.
evidence.limits: Assignment here indicates proposed affinity to H. floresiensis; it does not prove a complete ancestor–descendant series. Coordinates mark an approximate public locality, not a surveyed fossil position.

evidence.title: Mauer: Homo heidelbergensis type mandible
evidence.dateBasis: Combined ESR/U-series on mammal teeth and infrared radiofluorescence on sediments; quoted uncertainty. Internal years use 1950 minus the quoted age in years for display; rounded geological ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: The Mauer jaw anchors a widely used but inconsistently delimited species name.
evidence.limits: The age interval dates the find layer; it does not unite all Middle Pleistocene African and European fossils into one species. Coordinates mark an approximate public locality, not a surveyed fossil position.

evidence.title: Sima de los Huesos: early Neanderthal-lineage DNA
evidence.dateBasis: Rounded geological age of the fossil assemblage; DNA gives affinity rather than a direct date. Internal years use 1950 minus the quoted age in years for display; rounded geological ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: Nuclear DNA places the Sima hominins on the Neanderthal side of the Neanderthal–Denisovan division.
evidence.limits: Their mitochondrial affinity differs; one maternal lineage cannot stand in for the population history. Coordinates mark an approximate public locality, not a surveyed fossil position.

evidence.title: Dinaledi: Homo naledi in the Middle Pleistocene
evidence.dateBasis: Combined tooth US-ESR and overlying flowstone chronology; published depositional bracket. Internal years use 1950 minus the quoted age in years for display; rounded geological ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: A distinctive small-brained hominin survived in southern Africa during the broad period of early H. sapiens.
evidence.limits: These dates concern the Dinaledi assemblage, not every chamber or the lineage’s origin or extinction. Coordinates mark an approximate public locality, not a surveyed fossil position.

evidence.title: Denisova Cave: early Denisovan evidence
evidence.dateBasis: Rounded early fossil age in the cave chronology; sediment ages and fossil ages are distinct. Internal years use 1950 minus the quoted age in years for display; rounded geological ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: DNA identifies early Denisovan fossils in the Altai; the cave also preserves older DNA-bearing sediment.
evidence.limits: The marker summarizes an early fossil occurrence, not the molecular divergence date or continuous residence. Coordinates mark an approximate public locality, not a surveyed fossil position.

evidence.title: Baishiya Karst Cave: Xiahe mandible
evidence.dateBasis: U-series dates adhering carbonate, giving a minimum fossil age; timeline plots that boundary. Internal years use 1950 minus the quoted age in years for display; rounded geological ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: Ancient proteins identify a Denisovan-related mandible on the Tibetan Plateau.
evidence.limits: 160 ka is a minimum-age anchor; the fossil may be older. It is not an exact occupation date or a complete genome. Coordinates mark an approximate public locality, not a surveyed fossil position.

evidence.title: Harbin: Denisovan mitochondrial DNA
evidence.dateBasis: Published minimum fossil age; molecular analysis identifies affinity rather than directly dating the cranium. Internal years use 1950 minus the quoted age in years for display; rounded geological ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: Mitochondrial DNA from dental calculus links the Harbin cranium to early Denisovan maternal lineages.
evidence.limits: The plotted date is a minimum boundary and the city-area provenance is approximate. A mitochondrial sequence is not a nuclear genome. Coordinates mark an approximate public locality, not a surveyed fossil position.

evidence.title: Ngandong: late Homo erectus in Java
evidence.dateBasis: Bayesian model combines multiple dating methods and contextual animal remains, not direct hominin radiocarbon ages. Internal years use 1950 minus the quoted age in years for display; rounded geological ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: A dated Solo River bone bed contains a late occurrence of H. erectus.
evidence.limits: A youngest known sample is not the extinction date; the bone bed accumulated in flood conditions. Coordinates mark an approximate public locality, not a surveyed fossil position.

evidence.title: Liang Bua: Homo floresiensis
evidence.dateBasis: 2016 revised fossil and sediment chronology; distinguish fossil range from approximately 190–50 ka attributed tools. Internal years use 1950 minus the quoted age in years for display; rounded geological ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: The named Flores species is represented by small-bodied skeletal remains in revised cave stratigraphy.
evidence.limits: The older claim of survival to about 12 ka was revised; younger associated tools do not determine when the species disappeared. Coordinates mark an approximate public locality, not a surveyed fossil position.

evidence.title: Denisova 11: a child of two lineages
evidence.dateBasis: Approximate genetic age used in the 2018 study; direct radiocarbon established only older than 50 ka. Internal years use 1950 minus the quoted age in years for display; rounded geological ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: A female’s nuclear genome identifies a Neanderthal mother and Denisovan father.
evidence.limits: The rounded molecular age is model dependent; a fossil location does not establish where her parents met or whether she had descendants. Coordinates mark an approximate public locality, not a surveyed fossil position.

evidence.title: Callao Cave: Homo luzonensis
evidence.dateLabel: About 67 ka and at least 50 ka
evidence.dateBasis: U-series estimates on individual fossils, summarized as a display envelope; not all are exact ages. Internal years use 1950 minus the quoted age in years for display; rounded geological ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: Teeth and fragmentary limb bones identify a distinctive hominin on Luzon.
evidence.limits: Dates apply to sampled remains, some as minimum ages; the envelope is not an extinction interval or a demonstrated continuous occupation. Coordinates mark an approximate public locality, not a surveyed fossil position.

evidence.title: Chagyrskaya: Neanderthals in the Altai
evidence.dateBasis: Published dating range for cave deposits associated with the Neanderthal assemblage. Internal years use 1950 minus the quoted age in years for display; rounded geological ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: Fossils, DNA and distinctive tools support connections between this Altai population and western Eurasian Neanderthals.
evidence.limits: Similarity supports a dispersal model but does not reconstruct every stop along a route. Coordinates mark an approximate public locality, not a surveyed fossil position.

evidence.title: Baishiya Karst Cave: a later Denisovan rib
evidence.dateBasis: Published layer age from the site chronology; proteins provide lineage identification. Internal years use 1950 minus the quoted age in years for display; rounded geological ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: Proteins from the Xiahe 2 rib document a later Denisovan occurrence at the same Tibetan cave.
evidence.limits: The layer age is a depositional bracket; it does not supply a last-survivor date for all Denisovans. Coordinates mark an approximate public locality, not a surveyed fossil position.

evidence.title: Peștera cu Oase: a recent Neanderthal ancestor
evidence.dateBasis: Published calibrated radiocarbon range for the fossil; generations inferred independently from DNA segment lengths. Internal years use 1950 minus the quoted age in years for display; rounded geological ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: Long Neanderthal-derived DNA segments indicate a Neanderthal ancestor about four to six generations earlier.
evidence.limits: This individual’s approximately 6–9% estimate is not a population average; the analysis did not find substantial contribution to later sampled Europeans. Coordinates mark an approximate public locality, not a surveyed fossil position.

waves.title: Early Homo between Africa and the Caucasus
waves.dateLabel: Broad dispersal context by about 1.85–1.77 Ma
waves.summary: African and Caucasus fossil records require an early history of dispersal. Dmanisi supplies a firm Eurasian observation, with tools older than the main fossils.
waves.limits: The display window is a broad context, not the measured duration of one migration; neither exact origin nor direction of every population movement is established. Schematic geometry marks broad areas only, never a surveyed track or proven meeting location. Internal years use 1950 minus the stated age.

waves.title: A proposed later Neanderthal dispersal toward the Altai
waves.summary: Tool comparisons and genetic affinities support an eastern European source for the later Chagyrskaya population.
waves.limits: Dates describe the destination deposits, not the departure or travel duration; the intermediate line is an inferred geographic connection. Schematic geometry marks broad areas only, never a surveyed track or proven meeting location. Internal years use 1950 minus the stated age.

waves.title: Neanderthal–Denisovan parentage
waves.summary: Denisova 11 directly demonstrates a first-generation child with parents from the two lineages.
waves.limits: The marker uses the study’s rounded molecular age; it illustrates contact, not parental migration. It does not locate conception. Schematic geometry marks broad areas only, never a surveyed track or proven meeting location. Internal years use 1950 minus the stated age.

waves.title: Shared Neanderthal ancestry enters sapiens populations
waves.dateLabel: Main shared gene-flow interval modelled at 50.5–43.5 ka
waves.summary: A 2024 analysis attributes most shared Neanderthal ancestry in its sampled humans to an extended period of gene flow; other early individuals also record additional contacts.
waves.limits: This is a genetic model interval, not a dated route. The broad western Eurasian illustration does not identify an exact contact zone. Schematic geometry marks broad areas only, never a surveyed track or proven meeting location. Internal years use 1950 minus the stated age.

waves.title: Multiple Denisovan contributions to sapiens ancestors
waves.dateLabel: Model point estimates about 45.7 and 29.8 ka; large uncertainty
waves.summary: Genomes from Island Southeast Asia and New Guinea support contributions from more than one differentiated Denisovan population.
waves.limits: Playback connects two model point estimates, not a measured duration or one contact event. The study reports 95% ranges of 31.9–60.7 and 14.4–50.4 ka under one recombination model; other assumptions change the estimates. Schematic geometry marks broad inferred areas, never a surveyed track or proven meeting location. Internal years use 1950 minus the stated age.
